     - The model uses the encode-process-decode paradigm, with a task-based encoder and decoder. 
     - The task-based encoder embeds inputs and hints as high-dimensional vectors. 
     - The task-based decoder relies mainly on a linear decoder for each hint and output. 
     - The model uses a message-passing neural network (MPNN) as the processor. 
     - The MPNN uses the max aggregator and passes messages over a fully-connected graph. 
     - The model uses layer normalisation. 
     - The model uses a three-layer MLP with ReLU activations for the message function. 
     - The model uses a linear layer with ReLU activation for the readout function. 
     - The model uses a linear layer for the decoder. 
     - The model uses a softmax function for categorical, mask_one and pointer types. 
     - The model uses a logistic sigmoid for mask types. 
     - The model uses teacher forcing during training, but removes it in the final version. 
     - The model uses online samplers to generate new training examples on the fly. 
     - The model trains on examples of mixed sizes, n ≤ 16. 
     - The model varies the connectivity probability p of the input graphs for graph algorithms. 
     - The model varies the length of the pattern to be matched for string matching algorithms. 
     - The model uses soft hint propagation. 
     - The model eliminates static hint elimination. 
     - The model improves training stability with encoder initialisation and gradient clipping. 
     - The model uses a fully connected graph. 
     - The model uses a fully connected graph with neighbours j ranging over all nodes (1 ≤ j ≤ n).
